text:
anna (support): bumping eng-runtime — customer ACME-prod on dedicated pool d-78 reporting sudden throughput drop and big latency regression since 2026-03-17T09:05Z. p95 token latency ~2.3s -> ~6.8s, 429 spikes, throughput down ~65%. No app deploys from customer that we can see.

devon (eng-runtime): ack — can you paste cluster id, pool id, and a short grafana link / snapshot? any recent control-plane deploys?

anna (support): cluster d-78, pool d-78-eu-west, grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abcd1234 (p95 / avg_batch_size / batcher_wait_ms panels). first events at 2026-03-17T09:05Z. customer says they didn't change max_tokens.

mike (runtime): quick guess: tokenizer packing / pack-by-tokens off, causing lots of tiny batches + continuous-batcher idle window too long. can you capture these metrics: continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size, scheduler.max_batch_tokens, batcher_wait_ms, queue_depth?

anna (support): grabbing from logs and metrics: 
- continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size = 1.2
- continuous_batcher.idle_timeout_ms = 50
- scheduler.max_batch_tokens = 1024
- scheduler.pack_by_tokens = false
- queue_depth (avg) = 14
- batcher_wait_ms p95 = 1200ms
- autoscaler replicas = 2 (min_replicas=2 in policy)

mike (runtime): ouch. avg_batch_size 1.2 is killer. pack_by_tokens=false + small max_batch_tokens means many short requests won't be combined. Also I see per-request param max_new_tokens=256 from a sample request header — that can split token packing behavior.

devon (eng-runtime): also check autoscaler metrics — lina, any anomalies in metrics scraping? I remember a billing-agent restart yesterday caused our gpu_utilization exporter to return NaN briefly.

lina (sre): checking logs: indeed, at 2026-03-17T08:59:12 the metrics-scraper restarted after a credential refresh failed (billing-agent auth token rotated). gpu_utilization metric returned NaN for ~3m, which prevented scale-up decisions. autoscaler stayed at min_replicas=2. That plus inefficient batching = throughput collapse.

anna (support): customer also reported a weird billing API 401 earlier at 08:58, might be related. they saw a spike in usage cost because many small batches increased token billing overhead.

mike (runtime): mitigation plan — quick patch: enable token packing and increase max_batch_tokens to allow token-level packing, and reduce continuous_batcher idle_timeout so small requests accumulate briefly instead of flush. Quick commands (internal admin):

curl -X POST "https://internal-admin.api/pools/d-78/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduler":{"max_batch_tokens":4096,"pack_by_tokens":true}, "continuous_batcher":{"idle_timeout_ms":20}}'\

then restart batcher on pool instances:
for node in $(svc list --pool d-78 | jq -r '.[].node'); do ssh $node sudo systemctl restart continuous-batcher; done

devon (eng-runtime): before applying, can you repro locally with a load test? use this loadgen to simulate many short requests so we don't hit customer again:

# loadgen.py
import requests, time, concurrent.futures
URL = 'https://d-78.example/predict'
def send():
    requests.post(URL, json={"input":"hi","max_new_tokens":6})
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=100) as e:
    futures = [e.submit(send) for _ in range(500)]

run that from within staging to validate behavior. capture avg_batch_size / batcher_wait_ms.

anna (support): running patch now on a single canary instance (node d-78-node-03). applying config via admin and restarting batcher. will report metrics in 2min.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-215 created (severity: high) — assigned to eng-runtime.

mike (runtime): long-term actions:
- ensure scheduler default is pack_by_tokens=true for dedicated pools by default
- make max_batch_tokens auto-suggest based on sequence distribution (we can use eval job to profile)
- add a guard for autoscaler NaN metrics to trigger fallback scaling by queue_depth
- add alert for avg_batch_size < 4 sustained for 1m on dedicated pools

devon (eng-runtime): agreed. Also add guide in ops runbook: how to triage continuous-batcher issues + quick config knobs.

anna (support): can confirm canary change results: after config patch on node d-78-node-03 (pack_by_tokens=true, max_batch_tokens=4096, idle_timeout_ms=20):
- continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size (node-03) jumped to 19
- batcher_wait_ms p95 dropped to 120ms
- p95 token latency for requests routed to node-03 down to 1.1s
- overall pool throughput increased ~2.7x when canary traffic shifted

lina (sre): autoscaler fix: rotated creds for metrics-scraper and restarted. gpu_utilization exporter stable now. scheduling team to validate no further NaNs.

anna (support): rolling change to remaining nodes now. customer reporting restored performance, will monitor billing impact.

devon (eng-runtime): good job. follow-up: open a postmortem and include timeline (billing auth rotation -> metrics NaN -> autoscaler stuck at min_replicas -> inefficient batching config -> throughput drop). Also add config default change ticket.

mike (runtime): note for runbook: repro steps for engs: the staging loadgen above + curl admin config patch are reliable. example repro curl to simulate burst of small requests:
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -X POST https://staging.d-78/predict -d '{"input":"x","max_new_tokens":6}' & done; wait

anna (support): ACK. closing loop with customer, will attach grafana snapshots and incident link. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INC-2026-215 updated: status -> mitigated, next: postmortem required.

anna (support): final update to thread: after full rollout p95 token latency stabilized at ~1.05s, avg_batch_size ~17. Will keep monitoring 24h.
